NOVELTY STATEMENT  
Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme using vibration amplitude as the leading indicator for spindle chatter resonance.  
Departure: A tuned mass damper (TMD) with adaptive stiffness coupling to the spindle housing, absorbing resonant energy at the chatter frequency via inertial counterforce.  
Physics connection: Spindle chatter resonance amplifies vibration at the natural frequency; the TMD introduces a secondary mass-spring system tuned to this frequency, dissipating energy through mechanical coupling before it amplifies into chatter.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: TMD effectiveness ≈ ζ² / [(1 - f²/fₙ²)² + (2ζf/fₙ)²], where ζ = damping ratio, f = excitation frequency, fₙ = TMD natural frequency.  
Magnitude verification: Assuming spindle chatter at 500 Hz, TMD tuned to 500 Hz with ζ=0.1, effectiveness ≈ 0.01 / [(0)² + (0.2)²] = 0.25 (25% vibration reduction).

EXECUTABLE TEST

- Pass/fail threshold: Vibration amplitude reduction ≥ 20% (25% calculated).  
- Duration: 1 hour (steady-state operation).  
- Kill criterion: TMD is falsified if amplitude reduction < 20% within 1 hour.  
- Validation: Uses ALREADY-RECORDED vibration log; no new data collection.
